fundamentals.name: Datadog, Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Datadog, Inc. operates an observability and security platform for cloud applications in the United States and internationally. The company's products comprise infrastructure and application performance monitoring, log management, observability pipelines, synthetics, real user monitoring, product analytics, continuous profiler, database monitoring, data observability, LLM observability, error tracking, network monitoring, incident response, workflow automation and App builder, event management, bits AI SRE, cloud cost management, cloud security, code security, cloud SIEM, threat management, sensitive data scanner, and CI visibility. Datadog, Inc. was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

judgment.summary: Strong growth metrics and high gross margins are offset by a very high valuation and thin operating profitability.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimate by 18.3%; next earnings date is 2026-08-06.
positives: Revenue growth 32.2% YoY — robust top-line expansion.
Quarterly earnings growth 113.4% — significant profitability improvement.
Gross margin 79.9% — indicates strong pricing power on core services.
Total cash $4.76B vs Total debt $1.29B — healthy liquidity position.
Consensus analyst rating is strong buy.
negatives: Forward P/E 82.18x — valuation remains extremely high.
Operating margin 0.8% and Profit margin 3.7% — profitability is thin despite revenue growth.
Insider selling reported, potentially signaling a lack of confidence from management.
Beta 1.55 suggests higher volatility than the broader market.

news.paragraph: Datadog (DDOG) has seen mixed signals recently, with one report highlighting its growing importance while another noted a 2.5% drop following insider selling. Despite a recent 12.2% rally, questions about its valuation persist, with some analysts suggesting it may be overvalued. The company's strong revenue and earnings growth, coupled with a high gross margin, are positives, but a low operating and profit margin, alongside a high forward P/E, present tradeoffs.
